doc: /app/spec/PROFILE.md 1.1 `filters.randomize` `seed`: '`filters.randomize` gains an integer `seed` that initialises its random number generator. ... two runs with the same seed over the same input produce the same output order. Which permutation a seed produces is yours to choose and is not graded; that a seed reproduces its own permutation is. Upstream did not update `stages/filters.randomize.rst` at this release - its option table still reads `None` - so this paragraph is the statement of the option, and `development/release-notes/2.1.0.md` corroborates it.' That release note reads '`filters.randomize` now has a `seed` option to initialize the random number generator.' Three runs are used: seed 7 (a.las), seed 42 (c.las), seed 7 again (b.las). a.las and b.las must agree point-for-point, and that self-reproducibility is the whole of the graded contract (which permutation a seed produces is free). The three-run structure cannot distinguish a seed that is honoured from one that is merely accepted and ignored - a seed-ignoring stage also writes a.las and b.las identically - so c.las's role is only to show that a second seed value still shuffles the payload without changing it (Intensity sum/min/max), not to prove the seed was used.
